title_en: Beishapo Village Committee v. Administrative Committee of the Eastern Zone of Xi'an High-tech Industrial Development Zone, et al. — dispute over arrears of land acquisition compensation
ruling_gist_en: According to the provisions of Article 114, paragraph 2 of the Contract Law, if the liquidated damages agreed upon by the parties in the contract are excessively higher than the losses caused to the observant party by the breaching party, the people's court may appropriately reduce them upon the request of the party concerned.

full_text_en:
Beishapo Village Committee v. Xi'an High-Tech Industrial Development Zone East District Management Committee, et al. — Dispute over Arrears of Land Acquisition Compensation

【Ruling Summary】

In accordance with the provisions of paragraph 2 of Article 114 of the Contract Law, if the liquidated damages agreed upon by the parties in a contract are excessively higher than the losses caused to the observant party by the breaching party, the People's Court may, upon the request of a party, appropriately reduce the liquidated damages.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2003) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 40

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Beishapo Village Committee of Beilin District, Xi'an City, domiciled at Beishapo Village, Beilin District, Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province.

Legal Representative: Dou Yongqiang, Chairman of the Village Committee.

Agent ad litem: Li Changcai, male, born on December 8, 1940, residing at No. 69 Beishapo, Beilin District, Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province, member of the Village Party Branch Committee.

Agent ad litem: Wang Bingsen, lawyer of Shaanxi Wang Bingsen Law Firm.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Xi'an High-Tech Industrial Development Zone East District Management Committee, domiciled at Huoju Road, Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province.

Legal Representative: Lu Weifeng, Director of the Management Committee.

Agent ad litem: Li Jianming, male, born on December 12, 1958, residing at 3rd Floor, Unit 32, Building 18, Block 31, Hansenzhai, Xincheng District, Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province, staff member of the Management Committee.

Agent ad litem: Huang Yaying, lawyer of Shaanxi Fazhi Law Firm.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Xi'an High-Tech Industrial Development Zone Beilin Science and Technology Park, domiciled at Huoju Road, Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province.

Legal Representative: Lu Weifeng, Director of the Science and Technology Park.

Agent ad litem: Li Jianming, male, born on December 12, 1958, residing at 3rd Floor, Unit 32, Building 18, Block 31, Hansenzhai, Xincheng District, Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province, staff member of the Science and Technology Park.

Agent ad litem: Huang Yaying, lawyer of Shaanxi Fazhi Law Firm.

In the case of dispute over arrears of land acquisition compensation between the appellant Beishapo Village Committee of Beilin District, Xi'an City, and the appellant Xi'an High-Tech Industrial Development Zone East District Management Committee and the appellant Xi'an High-Tech Industrial Development Zone Beilin Science and Technology Park, the Shaanxi High People's Court rendered the Civil Judgment (2002) Shaan Min Yi Chu Zi No. 2 on December 16, 2002. The appellant Beishapo Village Committee of Beilin District, Xi'an City, and the appellants Xi'an High-Tech Industrial Development Zone East District Management Committee and Xi'an High-Tech Industrial Development Zone Beilin Science and Technology Park, being dissatisfied with the said judgment, appealed to this Court. This Court lawfully constituted a collegial panel and held a hearing on August 13, 2003. The agents ad litem of the appellant Beishapo Village Committee of Beilin District, Xi'an City, Li Changcai and Wang Bingsen, and the agents ad litem of the appellant Xi'an High-Tech Industrial Development Zone East District Management Committee and the appellant Xi'an High-Tech Industrial Development Zone Beilin Science and Technology Park, Li Jianming and Huang Yaying, participated in the proceedings. The case is now concluded.

After trial, the court of first instance found the following facts: Xi'an High-Tech Industrial Development Zone East District Management Committee and Xi'an High-Tech Industrial Development Zone Beilin Science and Technology Park (hereinafter collectively referred to as Beilin Science and Technology Park) operate as one team with two names. In 1991, Beilin Science and Technology Park, in accordance with relevant administrative documents and approvals from the Shaanxi Provincial People's Government, the Xi'an Municipal People's Government of Shaanxi Province, and the Beilin District People's Government of Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province, expropriated collective land belonging to the Beishapo Village Committee of Beilin District, Xi'an City (hereinafter referred to as Beishapo Village Committee) through the method of village dissolution and household relocation, and initially used 94.532 mu of land from Beishapo Village Committee. On September 30, 1997, upon the request of Beishapo Village Committee that it did not wish to dissolve the village and relocate households, the Beilin District People's Government of Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province issued the Approval Bei Zheng Fa (1997) No. 079 to retrospectively handle the land acquisition procedures for the land already transferred by Beishapo Village Committee to Beilin Science and Technology Park for use.

On April 27, 1998, Beishapo Village Committee and Beilin Science and Technology Park signed the "Land Acquisition Agreement," stipulating: ... 2. Beilin Science and Technology Park production area expropriates 94.532 mu of Caiziwan land from Beishapo Village Committee, calculated at RMB 126,000 per mu, totaling RMB 11.911 million. 3. Beilin Science and Technology Park shall be responsible for uniformly expropriating the living area (land located north of the Second Ring Road) within the planning scope as state-owned land, and after deducting land for urban greening and roads, shall return all of it to Beishapo Village Committee, and transfer the title certificate to the name of the Second Branch of Shuanghuan Company, which is under Beishapo Village Committee. ... 5. Beishapo Village Committee shall no longer raise any objections to the compensation already paid for original surface attachments. 6. Payment method: After the agreement is signed and sealed by both parties and becomes effective, Beilin Science and Technology Park shall make payment in four installments: the first installment of 20% of the total land price shall be paid to Beishapo Village Committee within 30 days after the agreement becomes effective; the second installment of 20% of the total land price shall be paid to Beishapo Village Committee before December 31, 1998; the third installment of 40% of the total land price shall be paid to Beishapo Village Committee before June 30, 1999 (at the same time, the land acquisition prepayments already paid by Beilin Science and Technology Park to Beishapo Village Committee before signing this contract and related expenses advanced shall be deducted); the remaining land price shall be paid in full before December 31, 1999. Beilin Science and Technology Park shall begin calculating interest on the amount owed to Beishapo Village Committee at the loan interest rate published by the People's Bank of China for the current year starting from June 30, 1998, until full payment, with interest settled annually. 7. Liability for breach of contract: If Beilin Science and Technology Park fails to pay Beishapo Village Committee within the prescribed period, it shall pay Beishapo Village Committee a penalty of 2/1,000 of the overdue amount stipulated in Article 6, paragraph 1 of this contract for each day overdue; Beishapo Village Committee shall properly handle matters with the villagers and shall not affect Beilin Science and Technology Park's normal construction and work. If villagers cause disturbances or obstruct construction, Beilin Science and Technology Park shall deduct a penalty of 2/1,000 of the amount owed to Beishapo Village Committee stipulated in Article 6, paragraph 1 of this contract for each day such event occurs. On June 26 of the same year, the two parties signed an "Agreement" stipulating that, taking other factors into account, Beilin Science and Technology Park shall compensate Beishapo Village Committee with RMB 210,000. Before the signing of the above agreement, Beilin Science and Technology Park paid Beishapo Village Committee RMB 1.375616 million in land acquisition compensation. After the agreement was signed, Beilin Science and Technology Park paid Beishapo Village Committee RMB 7.64 million in land acquisition compensation from May 25, 1998 to January 4, 2001. Beilin Science and Technology Park also paid agriculture tax on behalf of Beishapo Village Committee in the amount of RMB 77,160.85, and paid Beishapo Village Committee RMB 1.441538 million for green crops and surface compensation (excluding RMB 162,000 paid by Beilin Science and Technology Park to land contractor households of Beishapo Village in June 1991 for green crop compensation). During the trial at first instance, Beishapo Village Committee provided a "Reconciliation Statement" dated April 9, 2001, with Beilin Science and Technology Park, which recorded: As of March 30, 2001, Beilin Science and Technology Park still owed Beishapo Village Committee RMB 2.895384 million in land acquisition compensation. The above figures were confirmed as correct through mutual verification. Thereafter, Beilin Science and Technology Park paid Beishapo Village Committee RMB 4.3 million in land acquisition compensation on July 17, 2001, August 31, 2001, and January 8 and 9, 2002, respectively. In total, Beilin Science and Technology Park paid Beishapo Village Committee RMB 13.315616 million in land acquisition compensation, RMB 1.441538 million in green crop and surface compensation, and RMB 77,116.085 in agriculture tax paid on its behalf, totaling RMB 14.83431485 million.

Additionally, on November 16, 1993, Beilin Science and Technology Park and Beishapo Village Committee signed two identical "Land Acquisition Compensation Agreements" for the adjustment of land use between Beilin Science and Technology Park and Xi'an Environmental Protection Equipment Factory and for the expropriation of land for that factory. One of these agreements had an obvious error in the calculation of land costs, and Beilin Science and Technology Park had actually paid Beishapo Village Committee RMB 277,410 in land acquisition fees.

On May 8, 2002, Beishapo Village Committee filed a lawsuit with the Shaanxi High People's Court, alleging: In 1990, Beilin Science and Technology Park used 94.532 mu of land from Beishapo Village Committee before signing a land acquisition agreement. On April 27, 1998, the two parties signed the "Land Acquisition Agreement" stipulating the number of mu, land price, and also providing that Beilin Science and Technology Park would be responsible for uniformly expropriating the living area (land north of the Second Ring Road) within the planning scope as state-owned land, and after deducting urban greening and road land, return all of it to Beishapo Village Committee, transfer the title certificate to the name of the Second Branch of Shuanghuan Company under Beishapo Village Committee, as well as the payment method for land acquisition funds, interest on arrears, and liability for breach of contract. After the agreement was signed, Beishapo Village Committee fulfilled all contractual obligations as agreed, but Beilin Science and Technology Park failed to fully perform its contractual obligations, causing significant economic losses to Beishapo Village Committee. It requested a judgment ordering Beilin Science and Technology Park to pay the overdue land acquisition compensation of RMB 2.119946 million and interest of RMB 81,932, and liquidated damages of RMB 13.914275 million (as of March 31, 2002); to continue to perform the obligations stipulated in Article 3 of the "Land Acquisition Agreement"; and to bear the litigation costs. On June 20 of the same year, Beishapo Village Committee added a claim for a judgment ordering Beilin Science and Technology Park to continue to perform the obligations under Article 3 of the "Land Acquisition Agreement" or to pay Beishapo Village Committee RMB 5.3 million for the costs of obtaining a state-owned land use certificate.

Beilin Science and Technology Park argued that the claims of Beishapo Village Committee lacked factual, legal, and contractual basis and should be dismissed. The reasons were: Article 3 of the "Land Acquisition Agreement" should be an invalid clause. This clause changed the land use purpose in the approval documents of the Shaanxi Provincial People's Government, clearly violating the prohibitive provisions of the "Urban Real Estate Administration Law" and harming the interests of the state and society. According to Article 52 of the "Contract Law," it should be an invalid contract; Beilin Science and Technology Park had already paid RMB 14.99631485 million, not only fully paying the RMB 11.911 million agreed in the contract but also overpaying RMB 3.08531485 million; the penalty rate of 2/1,000 per day stipulated in Article 7, paragraph 3 of the "Land Acquisition Agreement" was clearly higher than the daily interest loss for the same period. It requested that, in accordance with the Supreme People's Court's standard for penalty for overdue payment at 0.4/1,000 per day and 0.3/1,000 per day in separate periods, the total penalty for overdue payment involved in this case should be RMB 1.220266 million. The actual loss from arrears or overdue payment is reflected in interest loss, and if the penalty for overdue payment is paid, calculating interest loss again constitutes double counting. It requested the dismissal of Beishapo Village Committee's claims and that Beishapo Village Committee bear the litigation costs.

After trial, the court of first instance held that Beilin Science and Technology Park, having obtained approval from the Shaanxi Provincial People's Government, the Xi'an Municipal People's Government of Shaanxi Province, and the Beilin District People's Government of Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province, had the subject qualification to expropriate land from Beishapo Village Committee. Although Beilin Science and Technology Park initially used the land of Beishapo Village Committee in advance, the two parties had signed the "Land Acquisition Agreement" on April 27, 1998, and the supplementary "Agreement" on June 26 of the same year. Except for Article 3 of the "Land Acquisition Agreement," which violated legal provisions and harmed state interests and should be invalid, and the provision for both interest and penalty, which constituted double counting, and the excessively high penalty calculation standard, which should be altered or reduced, the other clauses were negotiated equally by the parties and did not violate mandatory provisions of national laws and administrative regulations, and should be confirmed as valid. The two parties had reconciled Beilin Science and Technology Park's payments on April 9, 2001, and the payment facts confirmed in the reconciliation statement were accepted. The reconciliation statement did not provide for the liability for penalty and interest for the prior overdue payment by Beishapo Village Committee. Now that Beilin Science and Technology Park has fully paid the land acquisition compensation to Beishapo Village Committee, Beishapo Village Committee's claim for continued payment of land acquisition compensation and bearing interest and penalty was unfounded and should not be supported. However, after Beishapo Village Committee filed the lawsuit, Beilin Science and Technology Park was willing to accept liability for breach of contract in the amount of RMB 1.231311 million based on the Supreme People's Court's calculation standard for penalty for overdue payment, which was acknowledged. Beishapo Village Committee requested Beilin Science and Technology Park to pay RMB 277,200 in land acquisition compensation as stipulated in the "Land Acquisition Compensation Agreement" of November 16, 1993. The two parties signed two "Land Acquisition Compensation Agreements" for the same piece of land on the same day. Beilin Science and Technology Park had already paid land acquisition compensation under one of the agreements. Beishapo Village Committee's request for payment under the other agreement constituted duplicate compensation for the same piece of land, so its claim was not supported. In accordance with Articles 44, 56, 77(1), 114(1) and (2) of the "Contract Law of the People's Republic of China," and Articles 47(1) and (2) of the "Land Administration Law of the People's Republic of China," the court rendered the following judgment: (1) The "Land Acquisition Agreement" and the supplementary "Agreement" signed between Beishapo Village Committee and Beilin Science and Technology Park, except that Article 3 of the "Land Acquisition Agreement" is invalid and the stipulated penalty standard is excessively high and should be reduced, the remaining contents of the agreements are legal and valid; (2) Within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, Beilin Science and Technology Park shall pay Beishapo Village Committee RMB 1.231311 million as penalty for overdue payment; if payment is delayed beyond the period, interest on the debt during the period of delay shall be doubled; (3) Beishapo Village Committee's other claims are dismissed. The case acceptance fee for first instance was RMB 90,591, with Beishapo Village Committee bearing RMB 63,414 and Beilin Science and Technology Park bearing RMB 27,177.

Beishapo Village Committee and Beilin Science and Technology Park, being dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to this Court.

Beishapo Village Committee appealed, arguing that the first-instance judgment had erroneous findings of fact and improper application of law, and requested the court of second instance to ascertain the facts and amend the judgment according to law. The main facts and reasons were: (1) The first-instance judgment had erroneous findings of fact. 1. The finding that Beilin Science and Technology Park had fully paid the land acquisition compensation was untenable. The payment of land acquisition compensation should be calculated based on the payment method stipulated in the "Land Acquisition Agreement." Calculated according to Article 6 of that agreement, Beilin Science and Technology Park still owes RMB 2.119946 million in land acquisition compensation and RMB 81,932 in interest. 2. The April 9, 2001 "Reconciliation Statement" between the parties did not constitute a change to the penalty and interest clauses of the "Land Acquisition Agreement." Like each previous reconciliation, this statement merely confirmed the amount already paid by Beilin Science and Technology Park and did not involve the calculation of interest and penalties. The court of first instance's conclusion that the "Reconciliation Statement" did not stipulate penalties and interest and therefore did not support Beishapo Village Committee's claim for penalties and interest was untenable. The liability for penalties and interest was clearly stipulated in the "Land Acquisition Agreement," and there was no need for further stipulation. (2) The first-instance judgment held that Article 3 of the "Land Acquisition Agreement" was invalid on the grounds of violating legal provisions and harming state interests, but did not specify which legal provisions were violated or how state interests were harmed. This article does not violate the mandatory provisions of Chinese law. (3) The first-instance judgment's reasoning that both interest and penalty constituted double counting and therefore the interest clause was invalid was untenable. The interest clause is not a penalty clause but a clause on payment and method of payment. Beilin Science and Technology Park's payment of interest is performance of contractual obligations, not liability for breach of contract. Stipulating both interest and penalty is not double counting; interest and penalty are two different types of provisions. Various types of bank loans in China combine interest and penalty, and the law does not prohibit this. (4) Beilin Science and Technology Park's breach caused significant losses and instability in the village to Beishapo Village Committee. The liquidated damages agreed upon by the parties were not excessively high in relation to those losses. The court of first instance improperly handled the liquidated damages in this case.

The "Land Acquisition Agreement" stipulated that if Beilin Science and Technology Park failed to pay within the prescribed period, it would pay a penalty of 2/1,000 of the overdue amount for each day overdue, amounting to liquidated damages of RMB 13.914275 million (as of March 31, 2002). The court of first instance should not have directly applied statutory liquidated damages when the parties had agreed on liquidated damages.

Beilin Science and Technology Park appealed, arguing that the first-instance judgment's order in item (2) to pay Beishapo Village Committee RMB 1.231311 million as penalty was improper, and requested the court of second instance to set aside that order, uphold the other orders, and have Beishapo Village Committee bear the litigation costs for the second instance. The facts and reasons were: (1) After the first-instance judgment found that Beilin Science and Technology Park had fully paid and overpaid, and that Beishapo Village Committee's claim for continued payment of land acquisition compensation and bearing interest and penalties was untenable, it then ordered Beilin Science and Technology Park to pay Beishapo Village Committee an additional RMB 1.231311 million as penalty, which was contradictory. (2) The first-instance judgment's finding that Beilin Science and Technology Park was willing to bear liability of RMB 1.231311 million had no factual basis and was a misunderstanding of Beilin Science and Technology Park's first-instance defense. In its first-instance defense, Beilin Science and Technology Park clearly stated that its actual payment exceeded the payable amount by RMB 3.08531485 million. Although Beilin Science and Technology Park agreed to calculate the penalty at the standard of RMB 1.231311 million, it did not undertake to pay Beishapo Village Committee an additional RMB 1.231311 million in penalty beyond the amount already paid. Since the overpayment of RMB 3.08531485 million already included and exceeded the payable penalty of RMB 1.231311 million, there was no basis for paying an additional RMB 1.23 million in penalty.

This Court found the following facts upon second-instance trial: On May 11, 1998, commissioned by Beilin Science and Technology Park, the Xi'an Surveying and Mapping Institute surveyed the land belonging to Beishapo Village Committee located north of the Second Ring Road in Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province, which was in the living area within the planning scope mentioned in Article 3 of the "Land Acquisition Agreement." The survey concluded that the total land area was 90.387 mu, including 11.602 mu of green space, 36.937 mu of road area, and the remaining developable area of 41.848 mu. Beilin Science and Technology Park did not go through the land acquisition procedures for this portion of land, and Beishapo Village Committee and its subordinate Shuanghuan Company developed and operated this portion of land on their own.

Beishapo Village Committee acknowledged during the first-instance trial that Article 4 of the "Land Acquisition Agreement," concerning green crop compensation, did not specify a specific amount. In one version of the "Land Acquisition Agreement," the amount for green crop compensation in Article 4 was filled in unilaterally by Beishapo Village Committee after signing. The "Reconciliation Statement" formed by the two parties on June 1, 1998, confirmed that the over RMB 2.87 million paid by Beilin Science and Technology Park to Beishapo Village Committee from 1991 to April 30, 1998, included agriculture tax paid on behalf, green crop and surface compensation, and land acquisition fees.

Beishapo Village Committee, both in its first-instance complaint and second-instance appeal, claimed that Beilin Science and Technology Park still owed it RMB 2.119946 million in land acquisition compensation and RMB 81,932 in interest. During the second instance, it also claimed that Beilin Science and Technology Park owed it RMB 2.5507 million in overdue interest, but did not provide evidence to support this. Beilin Science and Technology Park provided evidence showing that the overdue interest it owed to Beishapo Village Committee was RMB 516,289.

Among the liquidated damages of RMB 13.914275 million claimed by Beishapo Village Committee, Beilin Science and Technology Park calculated that, according to the standard stipulated in the "Land Acquisition Agreement," the amount of liquidated damages was over RMB 6.2 million.

Both Beishapo Village Committee and Beilin Science and Technology Park did not perform the "Agreement" signed on June 26, 1998. Beishapo Village Committee did not refer to the contents of that "Agreement" in its first-instance complaint.

Other facts found by this Court upon second-instance trial are consistent with those found by the court of first instance.

Opinion of the Court: Beilin Science and Technology Park, after being approved by the people's government having the authority to grant approval, lawfully obtained the qualification to expropriate the rural collective land owned by Beishapo Village Committee. The Land Expropriation Agreement signed with Beishapo Village Committee on April 27, 1998, was an agreement reached through negotiation on a voluntary and equal basis, with genuine expressions of intent. Article 3 of the Land Expropriation Agreement stipulated that Beilin Science and Technology Park would be responsible for uniformly expropriating the land in the living area within the planned area as state-owned land, and then, after deducting land for urban greening and roads, return all of it to Beishapo Village Committee, and transfer the land title certificate to the name of the Second Branch of Shuanghuan Company, which belonged to Beishapo Village Committee. This changed the land use purpose designated in the land expropriation approval document issued by the relevant provincial people's government, violated the mandatory provisions of China's Land Administration Law concerning the use of state-owned land, and, without stipulating the receipt of consideration, returned the rural collective land to Beishapo Village Committee after expropriating it as state-owned land, thereby harming national and social public interests and violating the provisions of Article 52 of the Contract Law. The court of first instance correctly applied the law in finding that clause invalid, while upholding the validity of the other clauses. An invalid contract clause has no legal binding force on the parties from the outset, and since the content of that clause has not yet been actually performed, the parties need not return anything to each other. The expenses required for Beishapo Village Committee to independently develop and operate that portion of the land shall also be borne by itself. Beishapo Village Committee's claim that Beilin Science and Technology Park should continue to perform the obligation under Article 3 of the Land Expropriation Agreement or bear the costs of land transfer fees and related expenses of RMB 5.3 million for its independent development and operation of that portion of the land lacks contractual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it. According to the land acreage and unit price agreed in the Land Expropriation Agreement, Beilin Science and Technology Park should pay Beishapo Village Committee land expropriation compensation of RMB 11,911,000. Article 4 of the Land Expropriation Agreement stipulated seedling compensation but did not specify a specific amount. The Reconciliation Statement dated June 15, 1998, confirmed that the RMB 2,870,000 paid by Beilin Science and Technology Park to Beishapo Village Committee from 1991 to April 30, 1998, included payments for agricultural tax, seedling and surface compensation fees, and land expropriation fees. As of January 9, 2002, Beilin Science and Technology Park had paid a total of RMB 14,834,314.85 to Beishapo Village Committee for land expropriation fees, seedling and surface compensation fees, agricultural tax, etc. Pursuant to Article 6 of the Land Expropriation Agreement regarding payment methods, which provided for the deduction of land expropriation advances paid and expenses advanced by Beilin Science and Technology Park to Beishapo Village Committee, the land expropriation fees, seedling and surface compensation fees, and agricultural tax paid in advance by Beilin Science and Technology Park all constitute land expropriation advances and advanced expenses, and should be collectively included in the land expropriation fees. After reconciliation, Beishapo Village Committee recognized the fact that Beilin Science and Technology Park had paid a total of RMB 14,834,314.85. In its complaint at first instance and its appeal at second instance, Beishapo Village Committee claimed that Beilin Science and Technology Park owed land expropriation fees of RMB 2,119,946 and interest of RMB 81,932, calculated from June 30, 1998, at the loan interest rate published by the People's Bank of China for that year, as provided in the Land Expropriation Agreement. Beilin Science and Technology Park had paid a total of RMB 14,834,314.85 to Beishapo Village Committee, which already exceeded the RMB 11,911,000 payable under the Land Expropriation Agreement, so it did not owe any land expropriation fees. However, based on evidence submitted by Beilin Science and Technology Park, it was calculated that it still owed overdue payment interest of RMB 516,289. Without a determination of liability for breach of contract by a people's court or arbitration institution, and without the parties having negotiated the assumption of liability for breach of contract, the overpayment by Beilin Science and Technology Park does not have the nature of liquidated damages. A portion of the remaining RMB 2,923,314.85 could be regarded as payment of interest on the overdue payment by Beilin Science and Technology Park from June 30, 1998. In the first instance, Beilin Science and Technology Park did not make a request for Beishapo Village Committee to return the overpaid amount, nor did it do so in the second instance. This Court does not address this matter. Beishapo Village Committee's further claim that Beilin Science and Technology Park should pay land expropriation fees of RMB 2,119,946 and interest of RMB 81,932 lacks factual basis, and this Court does not support it. The parties' agreement in the contract that interest would be paid on overdue payments while also stipulating liability for breach of contract does not violate mandatory legal provisions. The loss caused to the party receiving payment by a deficiency or overdue payment is reflected in the loss of expected interest income. Beishapo Village Committee did not provide effective evidence to prove that its losses due to Beilin Science and Technology Park's overdue payment exceeded the loss of interest at the same loan rate. Calculating the amount of liquidated damages according to the daily rate of 0.2% agreed in the Land Expropriation Agreement, whether the RMB 13,914,275 claimed by Beishapo Village Committee or the over RMB 6,200,000 calculated by Beilin Science and Technology Park, both are excessively higher than the interest on the overdue payment calculated at the same type of loan interest rate published by the People's Bank of China for the same period, which was RMB 516,289. The standard for determining when the liquidated damages are excessively higher than the loss should be, according to the spirit of Article 114 of the Contract Law, whether the agreed amount of liquidated damages is excessively higher than the loss caused by the breach of contract. In this case, Beilin Science and Technology Park, on the grounds that the amount of liquidated damages agreed in the contract was excessively higher than the loss of interest suffered by Beishapo Village Committee due to delayed receipt of land expropriation fees, requested an adjustment. This is consistent with the conditions stipulated in the Contract Law. The court of first instance, taking into account the actual circumstances of the case and based on Beilin Science and Technology Park's willingness to calculate in stages according to the Supreme People's Court's standard for liquidated damages on overdue payments, determined a specific amount for the liquidated damages on overdue payments. Although this amount was higher than the interest loss, it fell between the agreed amount of liquidated damages and the loss caused by the breach, and was significantly lower than the agreed amount of liquidated damages. This was an adjustment to the situation where the agreed liquidated damages were excessively higher than the loss caused by the breach, which was a result of the people's court's discretion in accordance with law, and there was no error in the application of law. Where the parties have agreed on liquidated damages, such agreed liquidated damages should generally apply. However, when a party asserts that the agreed liquidated damages are excessively higher than the loss caused, the people's court has the authority to make appropriate adjustments by reference to a certain calculation standard, not directly applying statutory liquidated damages. Beishapo Village Committee's argument that the court of first instance should be corrected for applying the statutory liquidated damages standard instead of the agreed liquidated damages is not well-founded, and this Court does not support it. Beilin Science and Technology Park failed to pay the land expropriation fees within the payment period stipulated in the Land Expropriation Agreement. The court of first instance, having found that Beilin Science and Technology Park had overdue payment conduct and should bear liability for breach of contract, and upon Beilin Science and Technology Park's request, and in light of the actual situation where the liquidated damages standard agreed in the contract was excessively higher than the loss of interest on the overdue payment, ordered Beilin Science and Technology Park to pay Beishapo Village Committee liquidated damages of RMB 1,231,311 at the overdue payment interest rate published by the People's Bank of China for the same period. This was an act of adjusting the agreed liquidated damages that were excessively higher than the loss caused by the breach, based on the party's request, and there was nothing improper. Beilin Science and Technology Park's grounds for appeal requesting the reversal of the relevant part of the first-instance judgment are insufficient, and this Court does not support them. Beishapo Village Committee's claim that the first-instance judgment should not have adjusted the agreed daily rate of 0.2% for liquidated damages to the overdue payment interest rate published by the People's Bank of China for the same period, and its request for an order requiring Beilin Science and Technology Park to pay RMB 13,914,275 in liquidated damages, are not well-founded, and this Court also does not support them. In summary, pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, judgment is rendered as follows:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 90,591 is to be borne by Beishapo Village Committee in the amount of RMB 45,295.50 and by Beilin Science and Technology Park in the amount of RMB 45,295.50.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Cheng Xinwen

Acting Judge: Jia Jinsong

Acting Judge: Guan Li

September 2, 2003

Clerk: Wang Dongying

[Biography of the Presiding Judge]

Cheng Xinwen, senior judge: born in 1963, Master of Laws. Appointed as a judge of the Supreme People's Court in 1999.
